card.name: Caporales
card.tagline: Bolivia's most popular folkloric dance — choreographed in 1969, jingling bell-bottom boots, the modern Andean cultural identity dance.
card.profile: The Caporales is a traditional Peruvian and Bolivian dance originated in Los Yungas of La Paz. Caporales were created and presented to the public for the first time in 1969 by the Estrada Pacheco brothers, who were inspired in the character of the 'Caporal' who is the overseer of the black slaves and was usually mixed race, wore boots and held a whip, a dance that belongs to the region of the Yungas, Bolivia. The dance, however, has a prominent religious aspect. One supposedly dances for the Virgin of Socavón and promises to dance for three years of one's life.
